meetings.headline: Planning Board revised draft zoning bylaws for cluster, senior, and inclusionary housing for the 2027 town meeting
meetings.summary: The Planning Board held a working session reviewing the second draft of proposed zoning bylaw amendments -- cluster housing, senior housing, inclusionary housing, and a new minor site-plan-review provision -- aimed at the May 2027 annual town meeting. Members refined tree-species language, discussed submission standards, debated payment-in-lieu and affordable-unit percentages for the inclusionary bylaw, and set a plan to consult town counsel, brief other boards, and hold a public forum in the fall. No substantive votes were taken; the only vote was the procedural motion to adjourn.

budget_items.what_was_said: A member proposed new escalating payment-in-lieu percentages by number of units, meant to get the town closer to whole without erasing a developer's profit margin.

meetings.summary: The Lunenburg Planning Board held an off-cycle working session to draft language for four zoning bylaw changes: minor site plan review, inclusionary housing, cluster housing, and a new senior housing bylaw. The board worked through a consultant's draft site plan amendment, discussed how an inclusionary housing bylaw with a payment-in-lieu and affordable housing trust could work alongside a proposed senior housing bylaw, and revised numerous cluster-housing standards (acreage threshold, open space percentage, density, buffers, performance guarantees). No formal votes were taken on the bylaw language itself; the board reached working consensus on several specific provisions and set its next working session for August 10th before adjourning with no public comment offered.

budget_items.what_was_said: A board member cited a recent purchase by a housing trust as an example of how tight the local housing market has become.

budget_items.what_was_said: A board member described teardown and new-construction costs in town as context for why affordable inclusionary units are hard to produce without incentives.

budget_items.what_was_said: A presenter described a prior town in which the state eventually funded affordable senior housing units on town-donated land after a multi-year process.

decisions.decision: Drop the proposed C2 provision requiring full site plan review for minor changes near residential abutters, in favor of relying on the more easily amended site plan regulations.
Keep the inclusionary housing bylaw applicable to ANR lots for now, revisiting if a pattern of small estate-lot subdivisions emerges.
Reinstate a payment-in-lieu option and an offsite-unit option for developers triggering inclusionary housing requirements, with amounts to ramp up with the number of units.
Raise the single-family density cap in the cluster bylaw from two to four units per acre.
Keep the cluster housing minimum parcel size at 10 acres rather than lowering it to 5.
Add explicit language requiring the percolation test be completed before site plan review for cluster developments.
Reframe the cluster buffer as a non-disturbed area rather than a cleared buffer, with the planning board able to require landscaping if the area is already bare/grass.
Allow the required buffer area to count toward the cluster open-space percentage.
Remove letters of credit as an allowed performance guarantee for cluster developments, limiting security to cash, a AAA-rated bond, or a covenant.
Treat cluster developments as a single parcel with an exclusive-use area rather than individual lots, removing the need for a frontage standard.
Do not include an under-18 occupancy exclusion in the senior housing bylaw, so the bylaw remains eligible to carry inclusionary housing requirements.
Require native tree species in the landscaping/shade tree requirements.
Count only conditionable/livable space (not inaccessible attics) toward the senior housing maximum dwelling size cap.
Use a different parking standard than 1.5 spaces per unit for assisted-living-type senior housing, to be developed separately.
Hold the next working session on August 10th from 6:00 to 7:00 PM before the regular hearing agenda.

what_happened.line: The board continued two multi-lot subdivisions, Parmenter/Round Road and 860 New Westminster Road, to July 27 for more engineering and maintenance review.
Residents raised concerns about storm-water runoff toward Lake Shirley, driveway placement, and a possible wildlife corridor on Parmenter Road.
The board approved three smaller items: a duplex conversion on Reservoir Road, a driveway and storm-water change on Arbor Street, and a storm-water permit on Mass Ave.

why_it_matters: Homeowners near Parmenter/Round Road and New Westminster Road will see construction timing hinge on a maintenance mechanism (HOA or covenant) and a fire-system cistern review still being worked out.
Runoff and possible wildlife-corridor questions raised by neighbors could affect lot layout and tree clearing before those subdivisions get final approval.
The board is also weighing changes to its common-driveway and inclusionary-housing bylaws over the summer, which could affect how future subdivisions and duplex conversions are permitted.

The bulk of the meeting was spent giving detailed feedback on the draft master plan and agreeing on the town planner's 2026 work program, settling on four zoning amendments (inclusionary zoning, senior housing, minor site plan review, and a cluster-development bylaw) to pursue before the next annual town meeting.

budget_items.what_was_said: The town planner called the current fee schedule overly complicated and said he would bring a simplified version to the board.

budget_items.what_was_said: A DLTA grant from MRPC will fund a review of remaining developable commercial and industrial land against the town's older buildout maps, expected by end of summer.

budget_items.topic: Master plan consultant contract - final presentation
budget_items.what_was_said: The board discussed whether to require a formal final presentation from the master plan consultant, noting one is already included in the existing contract.

budget_items.topic: Capital Planning Committee / town budget

budget_items.what_was_said: Montachusett Regional Planning Commission business included approving member travel and allocating money to hire another planner.

The board settled on four zoning amendments to pursue before the next annual town meeting: rewriting inclusionary zoning, a senior housing bylaw, minor site plan review, and a cluster-development-by-right bylaw.
The scenic road bylaw and a town signage bylaw were pushed off to a second year of zoning work rather than pursued this year.

The continued hearing means the townhome project's fire-access and engineering questions are unresolved and will return for another public hearing.
Declining the right of first refusal clears the way for the Northfield Road land to be sold or developed privately rather than held or acquired by the town.

meetings.headline: Board declined to endorse a 35-lot Parmentor Road ANR over Fire Road 15's inadequacy, waiving refiling fees
meetings.summary: The board spent most of the meeting on an ANR for 10 Parmentor Road, ultimately declining to endorse it because Fire Road 15 (proposed frontage for a number of the lots) was found not to have sufficient width, grade or construction, while agreeing to waive filing fees if the applicant resubmits a revised plan within six months. Three smaller matters were continued to January 26 (30 Summer Street, Zero Reservoir Road, and a scenic road application at 1083 Northfield Road), and the board granted a one-year construction extension for the 485 Leominster Shirley Road battery storage project, plus routine committee reports including uncertainty over this year's capital budget funding.

what_happened.line: Board voted 4-0 to deny endorsement of the 10 Parmentor Road subdivision plan, finding Fire Road 15 lacks adequate width, grade and construction, but agreed to waive refiling fees if a revised plan comes back within six months.
Board granted a one-year extension of the construction start deadline for the 485 Leominster Shirley Road battery storage project, citing tariff-related delays outside the applicant's control.
Three other matters -- a storm water permit for 30 Summer Street, a storm water permit for Zero Reservoir Road, and a scenic road permit for 1083 Northfield Road -- were each continued to January 26.
Capital Planning Committee submitted its project rankings but said how much money will actually be available for this year's capital budget is still unclear.

why_it_matters: The 10 Parmentor Road denial means any subdivision relying on Fire Road 15 frontage cannot proceed until the road issue is resolved, though the fee waiver lowers the cost of trying again.
Residents tied to the 30 Summer Street, Zero Reservoir Road and 1083 Northfield Road applications will not get a decision until the January 26 meeting.
An unclear capital budget outlook affects which municipal projects the town can fund this year, pending the town's broader finance and staffing picture.
